opening.text: A lighthouse doesn't move. Storms come and the waves crash. The light stays where it is. Ships find their way home because it doesn't change. When we stand for truth, we become that kind of light for people around us. Our steadiness helps someone else find the way.

mainMessage.text: Standing for truth makes us a lighthouse. We stay steady so others can find their way.

blocks.text: **The light stays lit** The lighthouse keeper decides each night to keep the lamp burning. Standing for truth begins with a choice.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Dare to Stand Alone” from the October 2011 general conference.
Do we have the moral courage to stand firm for our beliefs, even if by so doing we must stand alone?
Choose, and stay lit.
**Strong against the storm** A storm tests a lighthouse. It doesn't test its wish to stand. It tests whether it is built well.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Dare to Stand Alone” from the October 2011 general conference.
Again, brethren, do we have the courage to stand strong and firm in the face of such difficult opposition?
Stand strong and firm.
**Sometimes the only light on the coast** A lighthouse stands alone on the rocks. President Monson knew what that was like.

Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all things, and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life—
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Dare to Stand Alone” from the October 2011 general conference.
Since that day, there have been times when there was no one standing behind me and so I did stand alone.
Sometimes we stand alone.
**Learning to say no** A lighthouse says no to the rocks. It warns, it doesn't bend. Saying no to what is wrong is part of standing.
Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.

President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Stand Strong against the Wiles of the World” at the general Relief Society meeting, printed in the November 1995 Ensign.
Thank you for the will to say no.
Say no when you must.
**Guarding against the wiles** The rocks are hidden in the dark. The adversary hides his tricks the same way. We need armor and light.
Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Stand Strong against the Wiles of the World” at the general Relief Society meeting, printed in the November 1995 Ensign.
Stand strong against the wiles of the world.
Stand strong.
**Never really alone** The lighthouse keeper isn't alone either. God is with those who stand for Him.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Dare to Stand Alone” from the October 2011 general conference.
May we ever be courageous and prepared to stand for what we believe.
Be ready.

story.title: Daniel keeps praying

blocks.text: A law was made that no one could pray to anyone but the king. Daniel knew about it.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
Daniel didn't make a show. He didn't hide either. He did what he always did. His steadiness was his stand.

story.title: Three friends and the furnace

blocks.text: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were told to bow to a golden image or be thrown into a furnace.

They said “but if not.” They would stand even if God didn't rescue them. That is what deep roots look like.

story.title: Elijah on the mountain

blocks.text: Israel was divided. Many were following a false god. Elijah called the people together.
And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.
Elijah stood almost alone. He didn't shout them down. He put the choice before them and let them see. A steady stand can help others decide.

story.title: The title of liberty

blocks.text: Captain Moroni saw his people losing sight of what mattered. He made a banner from a torn coat.

And it came to pass that he rent his coat; and he took a piece thereof, and wrote upon it—In memory of our God, our religion, and freedom, and our peace, our wives, and our children—and he fastened it upon the end of a pole.
Moroni named what mattered most and lifted it up. People saw it and gathered. A clear banner can call others to the good.

story.title: Abinadi stands

blocks.text: Abinadi was brought before King Noah and his priests. He was told to take back his words, or he would die.

Yea, and I will suffer even until death, and I will not recall my words, and they shall stand as a testimony against you. And if ye slay me ye will shed innocent blood, and this shall also stand as a testimony against you at the last day.
Abinadi stood alone and stayed true. One young priest, Alma, was moved by it and later led many to Christ. A stand can reach farther than we ever see.
